3.content: ... ... The Great Spirit too, which is in it, is like a wise

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶1:** The primordial Divine Wisdom [GAP-1] is as a great and exalted good whose interior treasures of love and truth have been seized by the power of falsity from evil. This good went forth to reclaim what belonged to it. In the same manner the [GAP-2] Divine Wisdom descended after its own truths-from-good out of the celestial degree, so that it might liberate them and recover its own spiritual riches, which had been dispersed and scattered among the falsities and evils that opposed it.

**¶2:** [GAP-3: It is as a celestial good] whose two essential faculties — the will and the understanding — were seized from it by [GAP-4: the power of falsity and evil. This good] went forth toward them to redeem them. In the same manner the primordial Divine Wisdom [GAP-5: yearns and] shines in the celestial degree on account of its two faculties, which had been severed from their origin. These are its living spiritual life that subsists in two powers — the will toward good and the understanding of truth — which, having each an interior and an exterior aspect, become four.

**¶3:** The vessel of spiritual illumination [GAP-6] is as a great penetrating power of truth [GAP-7: that pierces through falsity. And the Divine Proceeding within it is as a wise] ordering intelligence that adorns and sets in right order [GAP-8] all the truths that serve as protection and armament in the combat against falsity from evil.

**¶4:** The Divine Truth Proceeding is as a warrior who goes forth toward the offspring of the Divine Love itself — an interior good that has been taken captive by falsity through spiritual combat — and liberates it from the dominion of the opposing evils and falsities.

**¶5:** The Divine Mediation likewise is as an exalted good [GAP-9: that goes forth] on account of the spiritual riches [GAP-10: held in the] power of those in bondage to evil [GAP-11: so as to recover] these faculties of wisdom and perception [GAP-12: together with the] truths-from-good and their living spiritual life, so that they would [GAP-13: be freed, and that living good might] be brought forth from the state of captivity in which it had been confined.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The First [Man] is like a great distinguished man whose treasure has been taken away from him. He came to pursue his treasure. This is how the [First] Man too came after his sons from the heights, so that he might redeem them and retrieve his treasure, which had been scattered amongst his enemies.

[He is like a man] whose two sons were taken away from him by [the enemy. He] came out toward them to redeem them. This is how the First Man [yearns and] shines in the heights because of his two sons, who were separated from him. They are his living soul that exist in two powers, which makes four.

The ship [of the day] is like a great spear [that is cast against the darkness. The Great Spirit too, which is in it, is like a wise][crafts]man who might beautify and set aright [all] the armour for war.
The Living Spirit is like a combatant who might go towards a king's son who has been taken prisoner of war, and he redeems him from the hands of his enemies.

[The Amba]ssador too is like a great man [who goes forth] because of the treasure [in the] hand of his prisoners [so as to redeem] these light powers [and to bring them together with the] sons and their soul, so that they would [be set free, and that the soul might] be brought forth in the land wherein it was imprisoned.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies this as "primordial Divine Wisdom," which in the Kephalaia's natural register is "the First Man" — the editor's reading is correct.
The spiritual reading says "the [GAP-2] Divine Wisdom," which corresponds to "the First Man" in the Kephalaia — the editor's reading is correct and parallels the parable's subject.
The spiritual reading says "It is as a celestial good," which in the Kephalaia's parable register is "He is like a man" — the editor's reading fits the pattern of ¶1's parable structure.
The spiritual reading identifies "the power of falsity and evil" as the agent who seizes the two faculties; in the Kephalaia's natural register this is "the enemy," paralleling "his enemies" in ¶1.

The spiritual reading says the primordial Divine Wisdom "yearns and shines" — the yearning expresses the First Man's longing for his two separated sons/faculties, naturally preceding "shines in the heights."
The spiritual reading identifies this as "the vessel of spiritual illumination," which in Manichaean cosmology is the Ship of the Day (the Sun) — the editor's reading is correct.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "that pierces through falsity," which in Manichaean register is "cast against the darkness"; the spear metaphor naturally completes with its function of striking the enemy, followed by the readable text about the Great Spirit.
The spiritual reading confirms "all the truths that serve as protection," and "all the armour for war" is the standard Kephalaic expression — the editor's reading is correct.
The spiritual reading says "that goes forth," and in the Kephalaia's parable register the Ambassador, like the figures in ¶1–2, goes forth on account of what must be redeemed.
The spiritual reading says "held in the power of those in bondage," and "the treasure in the hand of his prisoners" is the natural Kephalaic expression for spiritual riches held captive.

The spiritual reading says "so as to recover," and in the Kephalaia's redemption vocabulary "redeem" is the standard term for recovering captive light, paralleling the redemption language throughout the chapter.
